topics.title: United States Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: The ordinary US naturalisation route combines five years as a lawful permanent resident with continuous residence, physical presence, English and civics requirements.
topics.scope: Ordinary adult five-year lawful-permanent-resident route; marriage, military service and citizenship through parents are separate.

facts.label: Permanent and continuous residence
facts.text: Age 18 or over, at least five years as a lawful permanent resident, and five years of continuous US residence immediately before filing.

facts.label: Physical presence is separate
facts.text: At least 30 months physically in the US within the preceding five years, plus three months in the responsible state or USCIS district.
facts.locator: General Eligibility Requirements — presence and jurisdiction

facts.label: English
facts.text: Basic reading, writing and speaking are required, with exceptions for qualifying applicants. USCIS does not assign a CEFR level here.

facts.label: Civics, character and oath
facts.text: Civics knowledge, good moral character, attachment to constitutional principles and an oath are separate requirements; consult current test and exception guidance.

facts.label: Form N-400
facts.text: Use USCIS Form N-400 and its current instructions after checking which naturalisation route applies.

limits: Continuous residence and physical presence are different tests. Absences and exemptions need individual review; this summary is not an approval or processing-time prediction.

topics.title: Hong Kong: Chinese Nationality Requirements
topics.summary: Hong Kong administers applications for Chinese nationality. Its passport listing does not represent a separate Hong Kong citizenship law.
topics.scope: Naturalisation as a Chinese national through the Hong Kong Immigration Department; right of abode and passport issuance are separate matters.
topics.jurisdiction: Chinese nationality administered in the Hong Kong SAR

facts.label: Legal basis
facts.text: Article 7 covers foreign or stateless applicants willing to follow China's constitution and laws who have close Chinese relatives, have settled in China, or have other legitimate reasons.

facts.label: Residence and local ties
facts.text: Officials consider right of abode, habitual residence, family, income, taxes, character and intention to remain. This guide sets no universal naturalisation residence-year threshold.
facts.locator: Factors to be Considered in an Application

facts.label: Chinese language
facts.text: Sufficient Chinese-language knowledge is a listed factor; no numeric proficiency level is specified in this guide.

facts.label: Other nationality
facts.text: Article 8 states that an approved naturalisation applicant cannot retain foreign nationality.

facts.label: Application evidence
facts.text: Use the Immigration Department's nationality application and provide identity, residence and applicable family or other-reason evidence. Each case is assessed on its merits.

limits: Do not describe seven years of Hong Kong residence as automatic Chinese citizenship. This page does not decide right of abode or entitlement to an HKSAR passport.

topics.title: India Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: India's ordinary naturalisation qualifications separate the immediately preceding year from a longer residence or government-service history, with statutory exceptions.
topics.scope: Ordinary Section 6 naturalisation for a person of full age and capacity who is not an illegal migrant; special CAA and registration routes are excluded.

facts.label: Immediately preceding period
facts.text: Residence in India or service of a government in India throughout the preceding 12 months, or a combination; special circumstances can permit limited relaxation.

facts.label: Earlier qualifying history
facts.text: At least 11 years of residence or qualifying government service in the 14 years before that final 12-month period, subject to statutory exceptions.

facts.label: Language
facts.text: Adequate knowledge of a language in the Constitution's Eighth Schedule is required. The Act does not express this as a CEFR level.

facts.label: Other qualifications
facts.text: Good character, qualifying future residence/service intentions and the other Schedule conditions apply. A certificate and oath are needed; qualifying time alone does not confer citizenship.

facts.label: Renunciation procedure
facts.text: This pilot does not establish the current document-level renunciation procedure. Do not treat this route as permission to keep another citizenship or an OCI card as Indian citizenship.

limits: The ordinary route is not a universal 12-year countdown. Registration, OCI-related eligibility, CAA and distinguished-service waivers require their own legal and procedural checks.

topics.title: UAE Citizenship: Routes and Limitations
topics.summary: UAE law distinguishes residence-based grants from exceptional talent provisions. Neither a strong passport rank nor residence alone establishes an obtainable second citizenship.
topics.scope: Selected provisions of the nationality law currently linked by ICP, in its 20 September 2021 consolidation. Operational availability and all implementing rules are not established here.

facts.label: Residence is not an automatic entitlement
facts.text: Article 8 permits a grant to other qualifying applicants after 30 years of lawful continuous residence, including 20 after the law, with livelihood, conduct and Arabic conditions.

facts.label: Exceptional categories
facts.text: Article 9 bis permits grants for investors, entrepreneurs, specialised professionals and talented people under implementing conditions. This is not an open citizenship-by-investment guarantee.

facts.label: Arabic and other conditions
facts.text: Article 12 bis lists Arabic, lawful residence, livelihood, qualifications, conduct, security approval and oath; specified exceptional applicants can be exempted from some or all conditions.

facts.label: Prior nationality
facts.text: Article 11 generally requires renunciation for naturalisation but excepts Article 9 bis acquisitions. Do not generalise this exception to every applicant.

facts.label: Practical availability
facts.text: The cited law does not establish an accessible application path or success probability for an ordinary foreign resident. These remain unverified in this pilot.

limits: Do not recommend this as an ordinary second-passport purchase for US citizens or other foreign residents. The statute and practical application availability are different questions.
The linked ICP consolidation is dated 2021; this is not a claim that all later implementing measures have been reviewed.

topics.title: Portugal Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: Portugal's ordinary residence route has different minimum periods by nationality, with a transition for applications pending before the May 2026 reform.
topics.scope: Ordinary residence-based naturalisation under the reform effective 19 May 2026; not a complete survey of descent or family routes.

facts.label: EU and Portuguese-speaking-country nationals
facts.text: Seven years of legal residence for nationals of EU member states or countries with Portuguese as an official language.

facts.label: Other nationalities
facts.text: Ten years of legal residence for nationals of other states; this is an eligibility period, not a processing estimate.

facts.label: Civic knowledge and other conditions
facts.text: The reform adds cultural and civic knowledge, a democratic-rule-of-law declaration, specified criminal and sanctions checks, and self-support requirements.

facts.label: Exact language standard
facts.text: This reform notice does not establish the current accepted language certificates or a CEFR level. Those details remain unverified in this pilot.

facts.label: Application date matters
facts.text: The notice applies the new rules to applications after entry into force; pending cases retain the previous law. It also flags implementing rules needed for practical operation.

limits: This review does not establish whether every implementing procedure is now available. Check the competent nationality service before filing.
Descent, marriage, statelessness and child-specific routes are not interchangeable with this ordinary adult route.

topics.title: Germany Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: Germany's federal naturalisation guide combines lawful residence, B1 German or accepted proof, civic knowledge and qualifying residence status.
topics.scope: Ordinary naturalisation as described by the federal government; personal exceptions require the responsible local authority.

facts.label: Residence and status
facts.text: The federal guide states more than five years of lawful residence plus a permanent right or qualifying permit. A study permit alone is not sufficient.
facts.locator: Requirements for naturalisation, first two bullets

facts.label: German language
facts.text: B1 oral and written German, or accepted German school, vocational or university proof.

facts.label: Civic knowledge
facts.text: The naturalisation or Life in Germany test normally proves civic knowledge; specified German qualifications can replace it.

facts.label: Other conditions
facts.text: The guide also requires self-support, criminal-record disclosure and commitments to the constitutional order and Germany's historical responsibility.

facts.label: Keeping another nationality
facts.text: German law allows a naturalised person to retain prior nationality. The other country's law must be checked separately.

facts.label: Where to apply
facts.text: Apply to the competent local naturalisation authority and check its document requirements before filing.

limits: Family co-naturalisation and statutory exceptions can change the result. This page does not decide individual eligibility or predict processing time.

topics.title: France Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: French naturalisation by decree normally requires five years of residence. Language evidence, civic examination and integration are separate conditions.
topics.scope: Adult naturalisation by decree for an applicant living in France; not nationality by marriage, descent or a decision on an exemption.

facts.label: Ordinary residence period
facts.text: Five years generally. Defined cases have a two-year period or no minimum; the applicant's main professional and family interests must be in France at the decree.
facts.locator: Step 1 — place and minimum duration of residence

constraint.cohort: Ordinary adult route; statutory reductions and exemptions separate

facts.label: French language
facts.text: The current proof guide requires B2 French, oral and written. Accepted qualifications/tests, accommodations and exemptions must be checked for the applicant's situation.
facts.locator: Nationalité française par décret — level and accepted evidence

facts.label: Civics and integration
facts.text: Civic examination, assimilation, professional integration and conduct are assessed separately from the language certificate.
facts.locator: Step 1 — assimilation, professional integration and conduct

facts.label: Application and decision
facts.text: Follow the official step-by-step service for evidence, submission, interview and the decree. Meeting a residence period does not guarantee naturalisation.
facts.locator: Steps 3–8 — dossier, submission, interview and decision

limits: Different routes and exemptions have separate evidence requirements. A French passport is a later document, not the naturalisation application itself.

topics.title: Ireland Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: Ireland's ordinary adult naturalisation route uses reckonable residence, including a continuous final year, rather than simply time since arrival.
topics.scope: Ordinary adult residence-based naturalisation; spouse, refugee, descent and minor routes need separate checks.

facts.label: Five years within nine
facts.text: Normally five years of reckonable legal residence in the last nine, including the continuous year immediately before applying.

facts.label: Final-year absences
facts.text: The guide allows 70 days away in the final year, with up to 30 more only for exceptional circumstances accepted by the Minister.

facts.label: Reckonable permission
facts.text: Stamp 2/2A student periods normally do not count, but a discretionary exception covers certain dependent young adults who arrived legally as children. Gaps in permission do not count.
facts.locator: Time That Does Not Count; Reckonable Residence for Young Adults

facts.label: Language level
facts.text: No numeric language level is established by this pilot. Do not treat a missing level as a verified exemption.

facts.label: Prepare the application
facts.text: Check immigration-permission dates and provide identity and residence evidence for the required years through the official citizenship process.
facts.locator: Residency Proofs; How to prove your identity

limits: Reckonable residence and proof of residence are different checks. This is not an automatic entitlement or a processing-time estimate.

topics.title: Canada Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: Canada's adult citizenship route counts physical presence and qualifying status. Language proof uses CLB/NCLC, not an assumed European-language equivalent.
topics.scope: Adult permanent-resident citizenship grant; child, descent and exceptional routes are separate.

facts.label: Physical presence
facts.text: At least 1,095 days within the five years before signing, including at least 730 days as a permanent resident.

facts.label: Earlier residence credit
facts.text: Eligible temporary-resident or protected-person days count at half a day, capped at 365 credited days within the eligibility window.
facts.locator: Time as temporary resident or protected person

facts.label: English or French
facts.text: Applicants aged 18–54 need CLB/NCLC 4 in speaking and listening, subject to the official waiver rules.

facts.label: Test and oath
facts.text: Adults aged 18–54 must pass the citizenship test; adults take the oath, subject to available waivers.

facts.label: Tax filing and eligibility checks
facts.text: If required under tax law, file returns for at least three of the preceding five years. Permanent-resident status and prohibitions must also be checked.
facts.locator: Permanent resident; income taxes; prohibited persons

limits: Use IRCC's presence calculation and application instructions. Qualifying to apply does not guarantee approval; do not translate CLB/NCLC into CEFR without an authoritative mapping.

topics.title: Singapore Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: Two years as a permanent resident is an application threshold for Singapore's ordinary adult route, not a promise of citizenship after two years.
topics.scope: Adult permanent-resident application; spouses, students, children and aged parents have separately defined eligibility routes.

facts.label: Permanent residence first
facts.text: An applicant aged at least 21 can apply after at least two years as a Singapore permanent resident.

facts.label: Discretionary assessment
facts.text: ICA considers family ties, contributions, qualifications, age, family profile and residence history. Eligibility to submit is not approval.

facts.label: Language level
facts.text: ICA's cited eligibility page does not establish a numeric language level. None is asserted here.

facts.label: After in-principle approval
facts.text: Applicants aged 16–60 must complete the Singapore Citizenship Journey. Citizenship follows completion of the required formalities.

facts.label: National Service
facts.text: ICA highlights National Service obligations for male citizens and permanent residents, with exemptions and cohort-specific rules. Review these before applying.

facts.label: Official application
facts.text: Use ICA's e-Service and the relevant document checklist; family applicants must make their required declarations.

limits: Permanent residence must be obtained separately. This page does not establish permission to retain another nationality; review the linked multiple-citizenship policy and ICA's formalities.

topics.title: United States Tax Residence & Foreign Income
topics.summary: US citizens and resident aliens generally remain within the federal worldwide-income framework while abroad; reliefs and filing obligations need separate checks.
topics.scope: US federal individual income-tax scope, including citizens abroad and resident/nonresident aliens; not state taxes or a calculation of tax due.

facts.label: Citizens living abroad
facts.text: US citizens and resident aliens abroad generally report taxable worldwide income under the same federal framework as those living in the US.

facts.label: Tax residence for non-citizens
facts.text: The green-card or substantial-presence test can establish resident-alien status. The presence test weights days across three years and has exclusions and exceptions.
facts.locator: Resident aliens; Green card test; Substantial presence test

facts.label: Relief is not automatic exemption
facts.text: Foreign earned-income exclusions and foreign tax credits may help eligible taxpayers, but claiming them requires a US return and satisfying the relevant rules.

facts.label: Nonresident-alien treatment
facts.text: Nonresident aliens follow different source-income rules; do not apply the citizen-abroad summary merely because someone visits the US.

facts.label: Foreign accounts and filing
facts.text: Foreign financial accounts can trigger separate reporting. Check the IRS-linked FBAR rules and filing guidance rather than assuming no tax due means no reporting.
facts.locator: Foreign financial accounts; When to file

limits: No tax rates, filing thresholds, state-tax rules or individual treaty outcomes are calculated here. Multiple citizenship does not merge the tax rules of the countries involved.

topics.title: United Kingdom Tax Residence & Foreign Income
topics.summary: UK personal tax residence depends on the Statutory Residence Test, not passport ownership or a single 183-day shortcut.
topics.scope: Individual UK residence and baseline foreign-income treatment; special reliefs, treaties and individual liabilities require separate assessment.

facts.label: Tax year
facts.text: Residence is considered for the UK tax year, 6 April to 5 April, and may change from one year to the next.
facts.locator: Work out your residence status; If your situation changes

facts.label: Residence tests
facts.text: Consider automatic overseas tests, automatic UK tests and sufficient ties. Spending 183 days in the UK is one test, not the only route to residence.

facts.label: Foreign income
facts.text: Residents normally pay UK tax on UK and foreign income. Non-residents generally pay UK tax on UK income rather than foreign income.

facts.label: Moving during a tax year
facts.text: Split-year treatment has conditions; moving country does not by itself establish the applicable split-year case.
facts.locator: Your residence status when you move

facts.label: Check your circumstances
facts.text: Use HMRC's residence checker and detailed guidance with your travel days, work pattern, homes and family ties.
facts.locator: Get help working out your residence status

limits: This is the baseline residence framework, not a review of new-resident relief, domicile transitions, treaty residence, capital-gains exceptions or rates. Obtain advice for the relevant tax year.

topics.title: Singapore Tax Residence & Foreign Income
topics.summary: Singapore distinguishes residence, Singapore-source income and overseas income. Its general overseas-income treatment has important exceptions.
topics.scope: Individual income-tax residence and overseas-income guidance, not corporate taxation or a personalised effective tax rate.

facts.label: Citizens and permanent residents
facts.text: Citizens and permanent residents who normally reside in Singapore, apart from temporary absences, are tax residents under IRAS guidance.

facts.label: Foreign individuals
facts.text: Foreigners may qualify through 183 days of stay/work in the previous calendar year, continuous stay/work across three consecutive years, or qualifying continuous employment spanning two calendar years with at least 183 total days including adjacent presence. The last concession excludes directors, public entertainers and professionals.

facts.label: Overseas income
facts.text: Overseas income received in Singapore is generally not taxable for individuals, including deposits to a Singapore bank account; this is not a blanket exemption.

facts.label: Important exceptions
facts.text: Exceptions include Singapore partnerships, overseas work or business incidental to Singapore activity, work in Singapore for a foreign employer, and overseas Singapore-government employment.

facts.label: Taxable income and relief
facts.text: Taxable overseas income must be reported in its relevant category. Double-tax relief may be available when the same income is taxed overseas.

facts.label: Income year versus assessment year
facts.text: Assessment generally follows the income year: Year of Assessment 2026 concerns income earned in calendar 2025.
facts.locator: Income earned in Singapore is taxable

limits: Citizenship alone does not make an individual tax-free. Check work location, income class, residence, clearance and treaty rules; no rates or personal tax bill are estimated here.

review.notes: Independent review of all 13 topics and 67 facts against all 16 cited primary sources, opened by this reviewer. USCIS and Hong Kong Immigration required direct HTTPS retrieval when the browser fetch failed; their substantive eligibility pages were read. Checked residence versus physical-presence cohorts, France's B2 requirement, Portugal's May 2026 transition and unresolved implementing details, and the India Act's ordinary route separately from special CAA provisions. Required and rechecked corrections preserving Ireland's discretionary dependent-young-adult student-residence exception and Singapore's continuous-stay and 183-day tax-concession conditions; Canada's tax-filing wording was also clarified. UAE Articles 8, 9 bis, 11 and 12 bis were checked in both extracted Arabic and rendered PDF pages, and the PDF was independently reached through ICP's current laws-and-legislation listing. Approval of UAE facts is limited to the explicitly dated 20 September 2021 consolidation and does not establish an open application route, later implementing measures or practical obtainability. Tax topics remain baseline individual frameworks, not personal tax calculations. Missing language levels, India renunciation procedure and UAE practical availability remain explicitly unresolved. No visa evidence, statistical indicators, rendering, promotion or deployment is approved by this record. Candidate hash binds this approval to the reviewed text.
